matches.rationale: Both identify that the abstract's claim of 14.6% improvement is misleading. GT notes lack of statistical variability and overstated universality; pred_id 2 shows the 14.6% figure only applies to one specific comparison (Table 7 VideoCLIP) while other results show much larger gains, and notes the abstract's unhedged claims conflict with actual results.
GT concerns a fabricated 1892 Filippini reference about cooking eggs in the Introduction. None of the findings mention this citation issue or any historically implausible references.

Both identify inconsistency in how action embeddings (computed as state differences) integrate with the model's loss and prediction mechanism. GT notes Section 3.2's difference embedding lacks clarity in 3.1/3.3; pred_id 3 identifies the contradiction between discrete-space cross-entropy losses and SAGE cosine-similarity decoding.

GT concerns missing hyperparameter tuning details for baseline re-implementations in the Experiments section. None of the findings address this experimental protocol issue regarding baseline optimization.

GT concerns Table 1 lacking variance/confidence intervals for state recognition results. Pred_id 1 addresses Table 5 ablation inconsistencies, not Table 1's missing statistical measures. No finding matches this issue.
GT concerns missing ethical considerations and bias discussion in the Conclusion. None of the findings address ethical integrity omissions or responsible AI deployment concerns.

Both identify the contradiction about frame-level supervision. GT notes Section 3.1 claims losses on ground-truth labels while 3.2 states annotations are absent and uses pseudo labels; pred_id 3 identifies the same issue with the incomplete sentence about cross-entropy losses and the conflict with VLM pseudo-label pipeline.
GT concerns rhetorical inflation in the Introduction using terms like 'powerful' and 'promising pathway' without tempering expectations. None of the findings address this presentation style issue.

GT concerns Table 4 showing suspiciously minimal changes when increasing graph concepts from 5 to 15. Pred_id 1 addresses Table 5 inconsistencies, not Table 4's suspicious stability. No finding matches this issue.
GT concerns ambiguity about privileged information (action/object labels) during evaluation in Section 4.1 and Tables 1-2. None of the findings address this experimental protocol ambiguity.
GT concerns suspicious training time disproportion (8 hours ChangeIt vs 30 min HowToChange despite similar dataset sizes) in Section 4.1. None of the findings address training time inconsistencies.

GT concerns missing criteria/thresholds for VLM-based frame filtering in Section 3.1. While pred_id 3 discusses methodology issues in 3.1, it focuses on loss computation contradictions, not the frame filtering specification gap.

GT concerns claiming generalization to multi-action videos when only single-action datasets were tested. None of the findings address this mismatch between claimed and demonstrated capabilities regarding multi-action scenarios.

GT concerns rhetorical exaggeration in the Conclusion about integrating SAGE into foundation models and solving fundamental perception challenges. None of the findings address this presentation manipulation in the Conclusion.

GT concerns unexplained extreme performance drops for baselines (LFC, VidOSC) on novel objects/actions in Table 2(b) suggesting cherry-picking. None of the findings address this missing analysis of baseline degradation patterns.
